For Reviewers

Academic policies.

written once, honest about being a working framework

The Credit Hour

One semester unit is about 45 hours of a student's work over a 15-week term: one hour of instruction and two of preparation each week, or the equivalent in laboratory, studio, or placement hours. Every course page states its hours by week. The fifteen ten-minute days published for each course are its open spine, not the course; the rest of the hours are the reading behind the doors, the seminar or laboratory, the making, and the writing.

Grading

Letter grades A, B, C, D, and F, with plus and minus from A− to D−, on a 4.0 scale (A 4.0, A− 3.7, B+ 3.3, B 3.0, B− 2.7, C+ 2.3, C 2.0, C− 1.7, D+ 1.3, D 1.0, D− 0.7, F 0). Each course page lists its graded components and their weights. Transcripts require grades; the portfolio is the primary artifact, and it is what the annual gate reads.

Attendance and Participation

Seminars, laboratories, and studios meet in person; attendance is expected and counts where a course weights participation. A learner taking the open curriculum alone has no attendance requirement and earns no credit until the Institute is authorized to award it.

AI Use

AI-native, not AI-dependent. Tools are open in every course and studied as a medium: what was delegated, how it was checked, and why the judgment calls were the student's. And every course examines the human unaided, in writing, mathematics, or code, because the Institute certifies the human and must observe the human without the tools.

Unassisted Examinations

Every course names its unassisted examination on its page: when, how long, and what. They are sat with every tool closed and graded against the unassisted examination rubric.

Academic Integrity

Work submitted as a student's own is their own; sources are named, and machine assistance is disclosed in the account the course asks for. Presenting another's work, or a machine's, as unassisted work is a violation. A first violation is addressed by the instructor and recorded; a second goes to the academic standards committee.

Accommodations

Students with a documented disability receive reasonable accommodations in every course, including the unassisted examinations, arranged before the term begins. The open curriculum is readable without an account, and its pages are built to work with assistive technology.

Late Work

Made things have defense and exhibition dates set at the start of the term; they move only by agreement before the date. Weekly written work may be submitted up to a week late for reduced credit, as the course states.

The Annual Gate

At the end of each year, a portfolio review and a written and oral examination against the five outcomes. A student who does not pass a gate repeats the work the gate names before continuing.

Satisfactory Academic Progress

Good standing requires a cumulative grade point average of 2.0, passing each annual gate, and completing the Foundation's courses in sequence. A student below the line is placed on notice for one term with a plan; a second term below it ends enrollment, with the right to appeal.

Status

A working framework, not an authorized degree. SDIT is in its founding phase and is not yet authorized to grant degrees; where authorization stands is published in full. The curriculum is open and free to take.
